item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E4: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2042 date comes from…
item.description: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2042 date comes from the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance. That was wrong. The Port's 2017 staff report (Item 9B, p.7) puts the Schedule of Performance in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) between the Port and the developer, which is a different agreement from the Development Agreement between the City and the developer. The report says the developer must complete phase 3 within approximately 25 years of project approval, but it never states the year 2042; 2042 is Pier & Point's own arithmetic (2017 plus 25 years). It stays labelled a legal outside date, not an expected completion. Source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf.
item.source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E4: The date shown for this parcel comes from the Disposition and…
item.description: The date shown for this parcel comes from the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA)'s Schedule of Performance, which is separate from the City's Development Agreement. The Port's report gives only years after Project approval, and the calendar year shown is Pier & Point's own arithmetic from 2017, before any extension for delay. It remains labelled a legal outside date, not a forecast. Source: Port of San Francisco, Item 9B: Pier 70 Mixed-Use Project approvals, Sep 22, 2017 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Item 11A: Pier 70 28-Acre Site Project update, Aug 7, 2026 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf).

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E4: The 2042 date on this record was drawn as an expected completion
item.description: The 2042 date on this record was drawn as an expected completion. The Port's 2017 staff report calls it an outside date in the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance (Phase 3 within approximately 25 years of approval), not a construction schedule. It is now labelled a legal deadline and no longer moves this record's status on the map or the timeline. Source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf.
item.source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E4: Parcel E4's completion milestone now reflects that the 2017 DDA…
item.description: Parcel E4's completion milestone now reflects that the 2017 DDA lists the Arts Building with Phase 3 items tied to the office building on Parcel B-2, not Phase 2, and the year shown is only a soft placeholder because DDA dates are tolled and being reset. The map notes now give the D4D's designation (retail, arts and light industrial, with upper-floor office allowed) instead of 'Arts only', cite Port Item 12B for the 'arts building parcel' wording, drop an uncited brochure and a generic ground-condition list, and no longer claim the site was never subdivided by the Assessor. The Item 11A milestones are dated to the Aug 7, 2026 staff report, and image credits and licence notes no longer say 'adopted' where the source doesn't. The D4D citation no longer calls it an 'adopted' document, and the Mayor's signing entry now states the Board of Supervisors' first-reading vote on Oct 31, 2017 and final passage on Nov 14, 2017. Source: Port of San Francisco, Port Commission Item 9B staff report, 2017-09-22 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Port Commission Item 11A staff report, 2026-08-07 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Pier 70 SUD Design for Development, updated 2022-04-26 (https://www.sfport.com/media/8123/download?inline=); Port of San Francisco, Port Commission Item 12B and Resolution 20-07, 2020-02 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Documents/Item%2012B%20Pier%2070%20Parcels%20E2%20and%20A.pdf); San Francisco Board of Supervisors, Ordinance No. 224-17 (https://sfbos.org/sites/default/files/o0224-17.pdf).

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Parcel E4: Port staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) for the… (Aug 7, 2026)
item.description: Port staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) for the Aug 11, 2026 Port Commission meeting (informational item 11A) describes proposed DDA amendments: parcel-specific outside dates, a Project-wide affordable rate of no less than 20% (327 stand-alone affordable units kept), 65-to-90 ft height increases on certain residential parcels, developer return cut from 18% to 14%, and a new phasing plan (Aug 7, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Parcel E4: Port staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) proposes a… (Aug 7, 2026)
item.description: Port staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) proposes a DDA amendment: change the zoning of Parcel E4 to allow residential use if an arts facility is infeasible, with Noonan Building tenants' replacement space provided in other buildings; this and 65-to-90 ft height increases 'could result in an additional 600 homes on site' (Aug 7, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel E4: Port Commission: Port staff and the developer are… (~Dec 2026)
item.description: Port Commission: Port staff and the developer are drafting amendments to the DDA and related transaction documents "for consideration by the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors by the end of this year or early next year" (Item 11A, memo of Aug 7, 2026, p.2 and p.6). The source gives no hearing date. The date shown is the early end of that window (December 2026); "early next year" falls in 2027. The same report proposes extending the term of the DDA, Development Agreement and Master Lease by 5 years. (~Dec 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel E4: Then the Board of Supervisors: the same amendments are… (~Dec 2026)
item.description: Then the Board of Supervisors: the same amendments are to go to the Board of Supervisors in the same window (Item 11A, p.6: "for consideration by the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors by the end of this year or early next year"). The source gives no separate date or order for the Board. The date shown is the early end of the window; "early next year" falls in 2027. (~Dec 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel E4: No completion date is sourced for the Arts Building on E4 (~2042)
item.description: No completion date is sourced for the Arts Building on E4. The DDA lists it among Phase 3 items (Port Item 9B, Table A, p.8: VDDA no later than the TCO for Building B2; Table 3: construction within three years after completing the office building on Parcel B-2), while the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan groups E4 with E1 and Building 21 in subphase 2C. 2042 is shown only as the outermost bound: Pier & Point's arithmetic for the DDA's Phase 3 outside date (approximately 25 years after Project approval; the Port's report states no calendar year) (~2042). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Parcel E4: Brookfield halts construction on the 28-Acre Site: The… (~Apr 2022)
item.description: Brookfield halts construction on the 28-Acre Site: The Real Deal (Apr 27, 2022, citing the San Francisco Business Times) reports 'Brookfield has halted construction' because of economic conditions, and Bisnow (Oct 20, 2022) reports that after the first phase's infrastructure and roadwork were completed 'progress stalled in April, with officials citing market conditions'. The Port's Aug 2026 report says the balance of Phase 1 horizontal work, largely the parks, is still to be built, so this was not the end of all Phase 1 horizontal work (~Apr 2022). Source: The Real Deal (citing San Francisco Business Times), 2022-04-27; Bisnow (Joseph Gordon), 2022-10-20; The Real Deal (citing SF Business Times), 2023-04-17; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: The Real Deal (citing San Francisco Business Times), 2022-04-27; Bisnow (Joseph Gordon), 2022-10-20; The Real Deal (citing SF Business Times), 2023-04-17; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07
